aboutH2: Recovery Acres Calgary: 1835 House Men's Treatment in Calgary, Alberta
intro: 1835 House is a men’s alcohol and drug recovery centre located in a residential area of Calgary, Alberta. The House provides daily living and meeting space for thirty residents, in addition to day-program clients, counsellors, and staff. It is operated by Recovery Acres (Calgary) Society, a local non-profit organization dedicated to providing an effective substance abuse treatment program that minimizes disruption and cost to the individual, family, employer, and the community at large.
1835 House has been the start of a new life for thousands of men since our doors first opened in 1975.

pillars.title: 1835 House on 27 Avenue SW
pillars.body: 1835 House sits on a residential stretch of 27 Avenue SW, in the Marda Loop area of southwest Calgary, about 10 minutes from downtown. The building has a dark front with a big 1835 above the door, and inside there is a book-lined lounge whose walls carry rows of sobriety plaques, plus a dining room where residents eat together. The society says it serves more than 40,000 meals a year. Its women's program runs a few doors down at 1839 House, and the recovery housing units are one street south on 28 Avenue SW.

pillars.title: Extensions, Work and a Place to Live
pillars.body: The first 42 days are the core of the program, and men can extend one week at a time if they need longer. According to the society's charity profile, men who stay on are expected to find full-time work, and staff help with the job search and, when needed, housing. Recovery Acres also runs 15 beds of recovery housing for men who have finished treatment but still want to live with others in recovery. Alumni come back to collect plaques at 1, 5, 10 and 25 years, and the centre says more than 1,800 have received the one-year plaque.

pillars.title: Fifty Years of Men Helping Men
pillars.body: Recovery Acres began in Mission in 1973 and later moved to 27 Avenue SW, which is where the name 1835 House comes from. The program follows what the society calls the 1835 Recovery Model, written up in 2008: a respectful group setting, mentoring from alumni and peers, and counsellors on hand 24/7, many of whom have their own recovery. Individual sessions are with a certified addiction counsellor. Stian Rorstad is Executive Director, Cade Feist is Operations Manager and Makaela Smith supervises the counselling staff.

location.heading: Recovery Acres Calgary in Calgary, Alberta
location.intro: 1835 House is at 1835 27 Avenue SW in southwest Calgary, in the Marda Loop area just south of the Beltline, about 10 minutes by car from downtown and roughly 25 to 30 minutes from Calgary International Airport. Okotoks, Airdrie and Cochrane are each around 35 to 40 minutes away, Red Deer is about an hour and 40 minutes up Highway 2, and Edmonton and Lethbridge are each roughly 2.5 to 3 hours.

faqIntro: Answers come from the centre's listing and its own website. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: How much does Recovery Acres Calgary cost?
faqs.a: Nothing, if you are an eligible Alberta resident. Recovery Acres is provincially funded, and the centre says no client ever gets a bill; you need a valid Alberta Health Care card. People from other provinces can ask about fees, which intake explains on the first call.

faqs.q: How long is the program at 1835 House?
faqs.a: The men's residential program is 42 days, or 6 weeks. Men can extend one week at a time after that. The Intensive Outpatient Program runs for at least 3 weeks.

1835 House is for adult men, 18 and over, who live in Alberta and want help with alcohol or drugs. You must be at least 5 days free of mind-altering substances before admission and commit to the full 42 days. Out-of-province callers can still ask, as exceptions are considered.

Detox is not listed among its services. The centre asks for at least 5 days free of alcohol and drugs before you arrive, so withdrawal needs to be managed first. Intake can talk through how to get there.

faqs.q: Do I need a doctor's referral?
faqs.a: No. You can call 403-245-1196 or fill in the intake form yourself. Doctors, social workers, probation, employers and EAPs can also refer, and most clients are admitted within days of a short screening call.

faqs.q: Where is Recovery Acres and how do I get there?
faqs.a: 1835 House is at 1835 27 Avenue SW, in the Marda Loop area of southwest Calgary. It is about 10 minutes by car from downtown and around 25 to 30 minutes from Calgary International Airport. The office is open Monday to Friday, 8 am to 5 pm.

Many men stay on with weekly extensions, and those who do are expected to find full-time work, with staff helping on the job search. Recovery Acres has 15 beds of recovery housing for men who want to keep living in a sober setting. Alumni are invited back for sobriety plaques at 1, 5, 10 and 25 years.

Yes, but not at 1835 House. The society opened 1839 House, a residential program for women 18 and over, at 1839 27 Avenue SW on January 2, 2022. Its Intensive Outpatient Program is open to all adults.

faqs.q: Is Recovery Acres licensed and accredited?
faqs.a: Yes. It is accredited by Accreditation Canada under the Qmentum program. Its Alberta licence for residential addiction treatment under the Mental Health Services Protection Act, number 10000414, is posted on its website and covers 1835 House, 1839 House and the 1822 House recovery units.

faqs.q: Is this the same as the Alberta Seventh Step Society down the street?
faqs.a: No. The Alberta Seventh Step Society at 1820 27 Avenue SW is a separate organisation. Recovery Acres Calgary Society runs 1835 House and 1839 House and can be reached at 403-245-1196.
